sub_graphs.title: EIP-1052: EXTCODEHASH Opcode Execution
sub_graphs.description: Models the runtime behavior of the EXTCODEHASH opcode when executed by the EVM

nodes.label: EVM Executing Contract
nodes.description: EVM is executing contract bytecode and encounters EXTCODEHASH opcode (0x3f)

nodes.label: Read Address from Stack
nodes.description: Pop address argument from stack, using only last 20 bytes (ignoring first 96 bits)

nodes.label: Lookup Account in State
nodes.description: Query the state trie for the account at the given address

nodes.label: Check Account Existence
nodes.description: Determine if account exists and is not empty per EIP-161 rules

nodes.label: Compute Code Hash
nodes.description: Calculate keccak256 hash of the account's bytecode

nodes.label: Result is Zero
nodes.description: Account does not exist or is empty, push 0 to stack

nodes.label: Result is Empty Code Hash
nodes.description: Account exists but has no code, push keccak256('') to stack

nodes.label: Result is Code Hash
nodes.description: Account has code, push keccak256(code) to stack

nodes.label: Push Result to Stack
nodes.description: Push the computed result (0, empty hash, or code hash) onto the EVM stack

nodes.label: EXTCODEHASH Complete
nodes.description: Opcode execution finished, 400 gas consumed

edges.label: Account does not exist or is empty (EIP-161)

sub_graphs.title: EIP-1052: EXTCODEHASH Gas Metering
sub_graphs.description: Models the gas consumption for EXTCODEHASH opcode

nodes.label: Gas Available for Opcode
nodes.description: Current gas remaining before EXTCODEHASH execution

nodes.label: Deduct 400 Gas
nodes.description: Deduct fixed cost of 400 gas (same as BALANCE opcode)

nodes.label: Gas Sufficient
nodes.description: Remaining gas >= 400, execution can proceed

nodes.label: Out of Gas
nodes.description: Remaining gas < 400, execution reverts

sub_graphs.title: EIP-1052: Account State Validation Logic
sub_graphs.description: Models the validation rules for determining EXTCODEHASH return value

nodes.label: Account Query Pending
nodes.description: Address extracted, account state needs to be determined

nodes.label: Check EIP-161 Emptiness
nodes.description: Check if account is empty per EIP-161: nonce=0, balance=0, no code

nodes.label: Check SELFDESTRUCT State
nodes.description: Handle accounts that have been selfdestructed in current transaction

nodes.label: Check CREATE Collision
nodes.description: Handle newly created accounts in same transaction

nodes.label: Account Non-Existent
nodes.description: Account does not exist in state trie

nodes.label: Account Empty (EIP-161)
nodes.description: Account exists but is considered empty

nodes.label: Account Exists with State
nodes.description: Account exists and is not empty

ambiguities.text: The distinction between 'non-existent' and 'empty' accounts returns the same value (0), but the text emphasizes this distinction.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume implementation should track the semantic difference for consistency with state trie representation, even though the return value is identical.

ambiguities.text: Behavior during SELFDESTRUCT within the same transaction is mentioned but not fully specified.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume EXTCODEHASH sees the pre-SELFDESTRUCT state until transaction completion, consistent with other opcodes.

implicit_assumptions.description: The state trie accurately reflects the account's code at the queried address.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Incorrect code hash returned could lead to false positive verification, enabling attacks on code identity checks.

implicit_assumptions.description: Gas cost of 400 is sufficient to prevent DoS attacks via repeated EXTCODEHASH calls.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Underpriced opcode could be exploited for state access amplification attacks.

implicit_assumptions.description: An attacker cannot find a collision in keccak256 to make different code produce the same hash.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Code identity verification would be broken, allowing malicious code substitution.
